answer: An agent economy resists sybils by admitting only keys a trusted issuer binds to one verified human: it signs each key once and checks a registry of real-world IDs so one person cannot enroll twice. A clone's cipher proves nothing without a human behind it; at the dawn of enrollment the registry is the denial point. Splitting into many keys fails: issuance, not compute, is scarce — its one-per-person check is crystal-clear, not guesswork. Cost grows with real humans, which an attacker cannot mint. It assumes the issuer stays honest and its ID registry resists forgery.
